negative_findings.description: Neither kibs.mk nor casys.com.mk publishes an explicit, machine-readable list of member banks / processing clients. KIBS pages describe services and counterparty categories (banks, treasury, HIF, Central Register, UJP) but name no institutions; CaSys names card schemes but no bank clients.
negative_findings.result_summary: Participant enumeration must be reconstructed from NBRNM system-description pages, MIPS participant counts (~20) and press coverage rather than from operator sites.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Who-supplies-whom in switching/issuing must be inferred indirectly, raising evidence cost and lowering certainty for partnership mapping.

negative_findings.description: nbrm.mk (National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to an automated fetch of https://www.nbrm.mk/mipsdd77afa6.nspx. Search engines index the site normally, so this is bot defence, not a dead site.
negative_findings.result_summary: All nbrm.mk candidates are recorded as blocked=true / unverified rather than dead; collection should use a real browser session.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The regulator holds the authoritative operator register, MIPS/KIBS/CaSys system descriptions and payment statistics — the single most valuable node in this cell.

negative_findings.description: Searches in mk and en for a distinct national card scheme (equivalent to Bancomat/BankAxept) found none. The nearest construct is CaSys / International Card System AD operating multilateral deferred net settlement for domestic-brand cards, alongside international schemes (Visa, Mastercard, Diners).
negative_findings.result_summary: No separate domestic scheme brand or scheme-rulebook publisher identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Removes a whole expected source category; scheme-level intelligence must come from CaSys and NBRNM instead.

negative_findings.description: Local-language searches combining Asseco SEE / Payten / Printec with Македонија, банкомати, ПОС and банка договор returned no MK-specific contract, reference or case-study page from these vendors.
negative_findings.result_summary: Vendor-side confirmation of MK ATM/POS estate suppliers not found in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Supplier mapping for the terminal and switch layer remains unevidenced; needs tender/procurement and bank annual-report routes.

negative_findings.description: No consolidated public source was found listing MK ATM/POS acquirers and their merchant-acquiring volumes per bank; NBRNM payment statistics appear to aggregate device and transaction counts nationally rather than by acquirer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Acquirer-level market shares are not directly published.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Competitive sizing of the acquiring layer will require bank-by-bank annual reports, a separate workstream from this cell.

brief: North Macedonia's payment-rail landscape is concentrated in three named operators: KIBS AD Skopje (retail interbank clearing, licensed instant-payments operator since Sept 2025, plus the OneID trust/eID business), the central bank's MIPS RTGS (live since 2001, ~20 participants, currently under an EU-supported replacement programme with a first test cycle in July 2026), and CaSys / Internacionalen Karticen Sistem AD — the country's only Visa/Mastercard-certified independent processor, also processing Diners Club, and itself a settlement system for domestic-brand cards. Operator websites are open and rich on service catalogues (switching, ACS/3-D Secure, personalisation, ATM/POS management) but publish no member or client lists, so participant and supplier mapping depends on the NBRNM cluster — which is the highest-value node in the cell yet returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching and must be collected via a browser session. The reliable secondary layer is MK-language trade press and associations (bankarstvo.mk, mba.mk e-bulletin, ecommerce.mk, ecommerce4all.mk) plus registry aggregators for ownership and financials; regional gateway/terminal vendors (Monri, Payten/Asseco SEE) are present but publish no MK-specific references. The largest open gaps are procurement channels around the MIPS modernisation and bank-level acquiring disclosure.
